A psychological warfare specialist who weaponizes illusion and terror, building illusory damage pools that kill enemies from the inside when they exceed current health. He thrives in Spirit Fugue, his Atmosphere abilities blooming into their full power the deeper into delirium he pushes.

A relentless finisher who specializes in the endgame of a battle — bleeding, poisoning, and dismantling the last enemy standing. Her kit accelerates toward that final isolated target, delivering the killing blow with empowered fury the moment her prey stands alone.

A paranoia-fueled controller who grows stronger the more enemies surround him, whispering commands into possessed minds and drowning the battlefield in retaliation. He turns enemy numbers from a threat into an advantage, feeding on the chaos of a crowded fight.

A dream-state manipulator who puts enemies to sleep and punishes them for it, while voluntarily slipping into incapacitation himself to trigger devastating illusory reprisals. He exists in a liminal space between waking and dreaming, exploiting both states with equal precision.

A dark confessor who consumes the afflictions of allies and enemies alike, converting their suffering into fuel for his own attacks. He turns debuffs into weapons — purging curses from his team and launching them back at enemies amplified and weaponized.

A moon-reading diviner who cycles the world's four elemental moons to deliver rotating team-wide enhancements. He adapts his kit to whichever moon is ascendant, shifting between fire, earth, air, and water buffs while wielding chaos, possession, and conditional kill tools between cycles.

An air-element strangler who degrades enemy action economy through asphyxiation, building Tired and Exhausted to leave foes gasping and unable to retaliate. He rewards pushing into Spirit Fugue for locked abilities and can sustain himself through near-death with Phoenix Soul.

An earth-element controller who buries enemies alive, locking them out of combat while setting up punishing follow-up strikes. His buried targets are temporarily untouchable but utterly helpless — patience and precise sequencing determine when they resurface and how much it costs them.

A cold and efficient finisher who locks onto the weakest enemy and refuses to let them escape. He specializes in culling, conditional kills, and overkill chains, ensuring that no wounded enemy survives long enough to become a threat again.

A water-element Reaper who weaponizes damage afflictions as fuel for conditional kills. He builds bleed, countdown, and hex in a chained cycle, then cashes out their accumulated value in devastating threshold executions — the more damage his curses promise, the deadlier his finishing blow.
Liminal Return — Resurrected allies cannot take direct damage for a brief period following resurrection, as though they have not fully returned from the void. Applies to all resurrection abilities.
Reckoning — Reckoning abilities scale their power based on the current value of a damage affliction on the target, calculating the full potential damage those afflictions represent.
Verdict — Verdict abilities can only target the enemy with the lowest health, representing the Executioner's role as the inevitable end for the weakest foe on the battlefield.

Burial — Burial is a variant of incapacitated that lasts for a fixed duration rather than ending on hit. Buried enemies cannot act, cannot advance their timer, and cannot take direct damage while buried. Burial ends automatically after its duration expires. Follow-up abilities allow the Gravedigger to capitalize on buried enemies through specific interactions.

Asphyxiation — Asphyxiation abilities build the Tired and Exhausted conditions on enemies, degrading their action economy through strangulation and air damage. Tired reduces an enemy's action options to two per turn. Exhausted, the upgraded condition, reduces actions to just one.
Breathless — Tired enemies cannot counter the Hangman.

The Four Moons — The four moons of the world cycle naturally, waxing and waning in intensity. Their benefits are team-wide, peaking when a moon is at its highest and fading as it wanes. Blood Moon enhances fire effects. Harvest Moon enhances earth and healing effects. Strawberry Moon enhances air and enhancement effects. Tidal Moon enhances water and control effects. Spirit Orbs are required to call a specific moon, and Reverse the Skies allows the cycle to be shifted.
Herald's Moon — A moon is active at the beginning of battle without requiring Spirit interaction.
Sin Eating — The Sin Eater purges afflictions from allies and himself, then weaponizes them against enemies. Consuming sin and turning it outward is the core of the Sin Eater's identity.

Oneiromancy — The Sandman applies incapacitation through dream-state manipulation, exploiting incapacitated enemies with follow-up abilities and existing in a liminal state himself. Voluntarily incapacitating himself turns danger into a powerful offensive tool.

Paranoia — Paranoia abilities scale their power based on the number of enemies currently present on the battlefield. The Whisperer grows more powerful when facing larger groups, rewarding engagement with full enemy formations.
Last Rites — Last Rites abilities interact with the final surviving enemy on the battlefield, representing the Mercy Bringer's role as the deliverer of the final mercy to the last standing foe.
Final Mercy — Whenever only one enemy remains on the battlefield, the Mercy Bringer immediately takes a turn with enhanced power.

Delirium — Delirium abilities gain enhanced secondary effects while the Gaslighter is in Spirit Fugue, rewarding the deliberate pursuit of that dangerous state. The Atmosphere suite each provides a baseline effect with a powerful Spirit Fugue bonus. Illusory damage is a stacking pool that kills the target if it ever exceeds their current health, causing a heart attack. Illusory damage can expire or be purged like other conditions.
Sustained Delusion — At the start of the Gaslighter's turn, if he is endangered, all illusory damage on enemies has its duration extended.

Gambits — Gambit abilities either work to great effect or have a negative consequence on failure.
Disarm — The Duelist specializes in rare and powerful disarm techniques. She can disarm opponents and take advantage after the target is disarmed.
Allied Coordination — For each ally that is ready at the same time the Phalanx uses her abilities, the more powerful they are. Some abilities require multiple allies to be ready simultaneously.

Succession — Succession abilities are dual-wield attacks whose second hit gains enhanced effects based on dual-wield attack speed. The faster her attacks land, the more powerful the succession payoff.

Bushido — Some Samurai abilities allow enemies to attack her first, though many also delay or reset the enemy's counter afterward. These abilities are stronger relative to the effect of the enemy's action, encouraging the Samurai to fight her most difficult foe.
Feints — Feint abilities can come in any action type and all compel an enemy and improve the Swashbuckler's parry chance. They grant a reaction on parrying and require a level of expertise.
Unstoppable Abilities — Dreadnaughts can use their defense to augment physical attacks, enhancing damage or causing other effects.

Scavenged Abilities — Scavenged abilities are prepared. On preparation, one of the six primary elements (air, earth, fire, water, light, dark) is randomly selected and locked in. The chosen element is displayed publicly and cannot be changed without consuming or disrupting the ability. This makes scavenged abilities less flexible than standard abilities but potentially more powerful, as the element is committed before targeting decisions are made.

Premade Concoctions — Premade abilities begin each wave already prepared at no resource or action cost. The first use requires no ammo and the prepared state cannot be disrupted in the conventional sense — only breaking the vial through combat disruption prevents it. After the first use, premade abilities must be re-prepared using the standard preparation system with a mana cost and can be disrupted during preparation. Premades are slightly less powerful than equivalent standard abilities in exchange for their zero-cost first use.

Accumulation — Accumulation abilities have two uses. The first use activates the ability and begins accumulating power; the ability grows stronger with each clock tick it remains active. The second use expends all accumulated power in a single discharge. The three Accumulator abilities (Beam, Burst, Storm) consume all active ammo on first use — the amount consumed and the active ammo type at that moment determine the base power and damage type when fired. Accumulating Detonation and Accumulating Trap accumulate power over time with no ammo cost.

Modifications — Modifications are toggled abilities that alter how the Tinker and her companions function. Each modification costs a move action to toggle on and a move action to toggle off. Any number of modifications can be active simultaneously. Some modifications affect only the Tinker’s abilities, some affect only the companion, and some affect both. Four major abilities — Modular Bomb, Modular Ray, Modular Trap, and Modular Beam — each function differently depending on which modifications are currently active.

Assistants — Assistant abilities are move-action enchantments placed on chosen allies. Each assistant type grants a different proc that fires whenever the assigned ally attacks. Multiple different assistant types can be active simultaneously on different allies. Each assistant type can only be assigned to one ally at a time — reassigning it to a new ally removes it from the previous one. Assistants that use ammo consume one ammo each time their proc fires. Assistants persist on the ally until reassigned.

Friendly Fire — The Bomber’s bomb abilities deal high area damage but apply the same damage to allies as to enemies. Base damage values are identical for all targets — there is no ally discount. Scaling abilities scale the same way for all targets.

Called Shots — Called shot abilities are prepared as a minor action. Each called shot names a specific target at preparation time and applies a powerful secondary effect to the first attack ability used against that target on the following turn. Without the capstone skill Quick Call, the called shot cannot be used and applied on the same turn — the minor action prepares the effect and the attack comes next turn.

Concoction Detonations — The Savant’s six concoction abilities are detonations with three phases. While placed on a target they apply an ongoing effect. Simultaneously, they accumulate power each clock tick from the moment of placement. When the detonation chain fires, the discharge effect scales with accumulated power. Concoctions also auto-detonate after a period determined by ammo consumed at placement — more ammo extends the active window, allowing greater accumulation and longer ongoing effect duration before the automatic discharge.

Siege Engine Operation — Siege engine companions (Ballista, Battering Ram, Catapult) can act on their own clock turns, but their base speed is extremely low. Without the Siege Engineer spending actions to advance them, they fire infrequently. The Siege Engineer’s move and minor toolkit exists largely to accelerate siege companions — quickening them, fuelling them with ammo for haste, and upgrading their next action via Siege Command.

Consequences — Consequence abilities generate Anguish on use and deal a deferred self-damage cost at the beginning of the Brute's next turn. Only the initial use generates Anguish; the deferred damage does not.

Reckless Abilities — Reckless abilities are powerful attacks that negate all active defenses and counter chances until the Raider's next turn. These abilities are further enhanced based on the total value of those active defenses at the moment of use.
Exertion — Exertion abilities have reduced accuracy. On a miss, the attack repeats targeting a random enemy and deals backbiting self-damage to the Berserker. This self-damage generates Anguish.

Rampage — Rampage accumulates as enemies are killed. Personal kills grant a higher Rampage bonus than team kills. Rampage enhances many of the Marauder's abilities, primarily scaling damage and speed.

Block Stacking — When the Viking has an ability prepared, each block made adds a charge to that specific ability. Multiple prepared abilities accumulate charges independently. When the ability fires, it consumes all stacks for enhanced damage or effect. Stacks are lost if the ability is disrupted.

Brink — Brink abilities become available for one turn after the Rager's cumulative damage dealt crosses a fixed threshold. This threshold tracks damage across multiple hits and turns. Once the threshold is crossed, unused Brink abilities expire at the end of the turn.
Purity Amplification — Purity abilities amplify in power each time they are used without triggering their cancellation condition. Each Purity has its own independent stack and cancellation condition.

Healing Threshold — The Cannibal can use threshold abilities when she has received enough healing that could actually be applied to her. Overhealing — healing above maximum health — does not count. The threshold accumulates across multiple heals. Some threshold abilities are prepared and activate automatically when the threshold is met; others require manual activation.

Massive Damage — Massive damage occurs when a single attack deals damage equal to or exceeding a set percentage of the target's maximum health. This threshold scales with target health rather than the Destroyer's stats.

Beast Forms are ongoing minor abilities that consume Anguish and provide continuous stat bonuses with additional effects. Only one form can be active at a time — activating a new form replaces the previous one immediately.
